title: Regression runs the project's optional quick tests after preflight and stops at a quick red
objective: When a project declares tests.quick, a red quick run ends the regression red right after preflight, before the full suite runs.
outline: scripts/testiface.py: add "quick" to COMMANDS right after "preflight", to DEFAULT_TIMEOUTS (600) and to BUILTIN (None); generalize the `cmd is None` branch of main() (today it writes preflight.log with 'built-in preflight: nothing to check' and returns GREEN) to write <command>.log; mode_of returns "quick" for quick; check_result needs no change (only `run` matches ids). devloop/core/testrun.py: docstring only (quick goes through run() like full; rc 0/1/86/2 map as for full). devloop/regression.py `_verify`: after a green preflight, put_live(..., "quick") and testrun.run(cfg, tree, "quick", timeout=<budget left>, keep_dir=os.path.join(logs, "quick")); RED, ENV and UNMEASURED end the regression with summary "quick: " + result.summary() and logs = quick's log dir; GREEN goes on to full with the budget left (pass a deadline instead of the precomputed full_timeout). An undeclared quick is green through the built-in no-op, so the live record may show stage quick for the fraction of a second the interface needs; that is accepted. No change to devloop/ticket_controller.py (a red report already starts the fixer), devloop/board.py, or board/config.json. Docs as in acceptance 11.

notes: Opener's check of when tickets meet (measured from the pool, 2026-11-21): the controller starts a group's regression about 20 s after its last member merges (g1: last merge #101 01:57:14, regression started 01:57:34; g2: #107 merged 02:30:19, regression 02:30:40). Earlier members do sit merged while later ones still run (g1: #100 merged 13 min before the regression). Decision: quick runs only at regression start, not at each merge. Why: while a group is open nothing can act on a red (the fixer starts only for a pr or fixing group, ticket_controller.advance_groups), the members still running keep moving the branch, and a quick run inside the issuer's integrate step would charge a cross-ticket red to whichever ticket merged last and add a test run to every merge. Regression start is the first point where all members meet; with quick there, the red comes seconds after it instead of after the full suite. agent-control's own config does not declare tests.quick: its full suite took 280 s on the last run, so a quick stage could save under 5 minutes per red, and its fast modules (the base set) already run at every worker hand-in; not declaring also leaves its regression as it is. Out of scope: running quick at each merge, parallelising full, any change to what a project's tests assert, any change to agent-control's board/config.json. 2. With `tests.quick` not declared (key absent, null or blank), `python3 scripts/testiface.py quick` exits 0 without running any command and writes $AC_TEST_OUT/quick.log containing "nothing to check" - the same built-in no-op an undeclared preflight has today (scripts/testiface.py main(), `if cmd is None`).
3. With tests.quick declared and nothing red, `python3 devloop/regression.py --branch int/g1 --out R` exits 0 and the fake test commands run in the order preflight, quick, full, once each.

4. With tests.quick declared and quick-red.txt committed on int/g1, regression.py exits 1 and full does not run; R has status "red", failures whose ids are exactly ["quick.red"] (the rows of quick's result.json), a summary that starts with "quick: " and contains "quick.red", and logs naming quick's log folder. The controller then handles the group as for any red regression (fix round; at devloop.max_rounds a "still red after" decision page carrying that summary).

5. A quick run that reports an unusable environment (rc 86) or cannot be measured (rc 2) ends the regression the way the same outcome of full does, without running full: exit 86 with status "env", or exit 2 with status "unmeasured"; in both the summary starts with "quick: ".

6. With tests.quick declared and green, a red full is reported exactly as today: exit 1, failures from full only (ids ["suite.red"] with red.txt committed), summary starting with "1 failing:" (no "quick: " prefix).

7. While quick runs, the regression's live record <worktrees>/runs/live/regression-<branch with / as ->.json has stage "quick"; the stages go preflight, quick, full. (The board's regression row already shows a stage it has no text for by its name, devloop/board.py:556 `LIVE_STAGE_TEXT.get(stage, str(stage))`, so the board label reads "quick" with no board change.)

10. Quick's run counts against devloop.regression_timeout_seconds: quick runs with at most the regression budget left after the slot wait, and full gets the budget left after quick (today full gets a budget computed before preflight).

11. The docs name the stage: devloop/README.md (the flow line near the top that says `regression.py (preflight + full suite)`, the bullet that starts `devloop calls only` - which also says `run <id>` must accept every id quick reports, as it already says for full - and the `regression-<branch ...>` live-record bullet, which lists stage `quick` between `preflight` and `full`), the docstrings of scripts/testiface.py and devloop/regression.py, templates/project-tests.example.sh (header comment and a `quick)` branch example), the Tests line of templates/project-CLAUDE.md, and bin/actl's `test <...>` help line.

request:
# Regression: catch cheap errors before the full suite, and rerun a few red cases once before calling the fixer

Reported by tabby_pool (T), whose full suite takes about 1.2 hours; the user agreed to both items (2026-11-21). Two tickets; both change devloop/regression.py `_verify`, so the second depends on the first (no parallel edits of one function).

## Item 1: a quick stage before `full`
T's measured symptom: cross-ticket conflicts in a group (a classification table, an allow-list, an escaping check) are caught by checks that run in seconds, but only inside `full`, so the group waits about 1.2 hours to learn it, and each fix round waits the same again.

Wanted:
- A new optional test command `quick` in board/config.json `tests`, declared like the other commands (scripts/testiface.py COMMANDS, DEFAULT_TIMEOUTS, `actl test quick` rehearses it, docs). The project decides what it runs (its fast static and table checks). It reports rows like `run`/`full` (result.json rows with status fail/error). Not declared: the stage is skipped and nothing else changes (agent-control's own config may declare it or not; say which and why).
- Regression runs preflight, then quick, then full. Quick red: the regression ends red at once with quick's failures (the same result.json shape: status red, failures, summary naming the quick stage), full does not run, and the controller starts the fixer as for any red. Quick environment/unmeasured outcomes are handled like the same outcomes of full. The live record shows the stage (`quick`), and the board's stage label shows it.
- Opener: check when the controller starts a group's regression relative to when its tickets are merged onto the integration branch. If regression starts as soon as the last member merges, the quick stage at regression start is the earliest point where tickets of one group meet, and that is enough. If tickets sit merged on the branch long before regression starts, say so in the ticket and decide whether quick should also run at each merge; prefer the simpler design and write the reason.
- removes: waiting for the full suite to learn about an error a seconds-long check finds.

## Item 2: rerun a few red cases once before the fixer
T's measured symptom: an intermittent failure (a browser connection timeout) turns the whole regression red and burns a fix round: a fixer agent is started for a case that passes when run again.

Wanted:
- When full (or quick) is red with at most 5 failing cases, regression reruns exactly those cases once with the project's `run <ids>` on the same tree, inside the same regression time limit and machine slot. A case red again stays red. A case that passes on the rerun is "flaky".
- All failing cases pass on the rerun: the regression is green, and its result names the flaky cases (a new `flaky` list in result.json: id, first failure's message). Some still red: the regression is red with only the still-red cases in `failures`, plus the `flaky` list; the fixer gets only the still-red cases. More than 5 failures: no rerun (that is not a flake).
- Flaky cases are never silent: the group keeps the list (group event), and the landed page (or the red/decision page) names them so someone can make the test robust. The memory rule stands that agents must not hide a flaky test with sleeps or retries in the test itself; this rerun is the gate's one second look, not a fix.
- removes: a fix round (an agent run plus another full suite) spent on a case that passes when run again.

## Both
- Out of scope: rerunning only the failed cases after a fix round instead of the full suite (the fixer already runs the failing tests itself before handing back; the user did not ask for it), parallelising full, any change to what T's tests assert.
- Tests go in the regression area's own test file (tests_devloop/test_regression_fixer.py) or a new file, using the shared helpers in tests_devloop/loop_harness.py and the fake test commands; never in a catch-all file. Each case should run in se
